newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by projections for light packer demand following two days of hefty hog marketings, livestock dealers said.

The marketings supplied more than adequate live inventory and were spurred by price advances earlier in the week which has pushed interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top hog prices at the plant to $61.50 on Wednesday, they said.
Top interior hog prices at the plant on Thursday closed $1.00 lower at $60.50 and were expected steady to $0.50 lower on Friday, the dealers said.
Illinois top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen steady at $60.00 after slipping $0.50 on Thursday.
Indiana/Ohio top hog prices were seen unchanged at $60.50 following a $0.50 decline Thursday.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog marketings on Wednesday were 113,000 head, well above the estimate of 105,000, USDA reported. Thursday's estimate was 105,000 head.

Marketings this week have exceeded estimates due to lower than expected humidity and cool morning temperatures in much of the Midwest, which have allowed farmers a chance to sort and ship hogs, several livestock dealers said.
